title: Close-up of labelled device with multiple glass tubes and sensor domes
objects_and_counts: A rectangular top housing with the visible engraved label 'LAVENDER' on its side is present in the upper-left quadrant.

At least four vertical clear glass tubes are visible hanging from the housing: one at far left is partly cropped, two central tubes are fully visible, and one at right is partially visible (total visible minimum = 4).

Four round white domed components with honeycomb-like internal faceted patterns (possibly sensor or diffuser caps) are visible mounted around the underside perimeter of the top housing: two near the right edge, one near the center-left area, and one near the far left (some are partly cropped).
Multiple metal lamp holders or tube sockets are visible at the tube tops where each glass tube connects to the housing; at least three sockets are visible corresponding to the visible tubes.
One vertical glass tube shows printed text and markings along its length (see visible_text) and contains internal metal electrode structures visible inside the glass.
spatial_relations: The labelled rectangular housing sits at the top of the image; the engraving 'LAVENDER' is on the left side of that housing.
Clear glass tubes hang vertically down from the underside of the housing; their top ends insert into metal sockets fixed to the housing underside.
White round domed components are arranged around the underside perimeter of the housing, positioned between or adjacent to the glass tube sockets.
A red background fills the out-of-focus area behind the device; the device is foregrounded and occupies the central and upper regions of the image.
One glass tube with visible printed text is located toward the front-center of the image; a partly cropped tube is at the far left edge of the frame.
colours_and_materials: The top housing appears light grey or off-white with a smooth, slightly metallic or molded plastic finish.
The domed sensor/diffuser caps are white plastic with a faceted internal pattern visible.
The vertical tubes are transparent glass showing internal metal components.
Visible metal sockets and small metal fittings appear silver/metallic and show some darker oxidation or discoloration near the tube connections.
Background is predominantly out-of-focus red, which contrasts with the pale housing and clear glass.
